notes: The verdicts and key numbers are accurate, and the recommended checks are actionable.

defects.quote: The run-level PASS reflects the existence of a verified bounded load (197 users)
defects.why: The evidence does not establish that the verified bound alone caused the run-level PASS verdict.
Knee detection is a fixed product limitation and is not an operator step needed to obtain the bound.
The throughput aggregate does not establish what caused the observed request rate.

defects.quote: stage-length assertions beyond the 30-cell summaries are not verified here
defects.why: The stage window start and end timestamps in the evidence establish each stage’s duration.

notes: Several useful checks are mixed with an incorrect account of the verdict and an invalid knee-detector recommendation.

defects.quote: Overall there are 0 errors across 3601 checkout samples
defects.why: Matching overall and checkout aggregates do not establish that they describe the same samples.
The whole-run p95 is 417 ms; only p99 is 420 ms.

defects.quote: Segment stage-3 samples by latency bucket and by per-10s cell to quantify how many observations exceed 250 ms and what drives the 1500 ms max
defects.why: The 1500 ms maximum is a whole-run aggregate and is not attributed to stage-3.
The aggregates do not show how many samples reached the maximum.

missing_facts: Whole-run latency p95 is 417 ms, not 420 ms.
notes: The capacity advice is useful, but the response misstates a latency number and assigns whole-run data to stage-3.

defects.quote: if generator overload caused the stage-3 latency breach, the diagnostic guard would be expected to fail
defects.why: A passing generator CPU guard does not establish that other forms of generator overload would be detected.
The verified failing stage contributes the upper_exclusive value of 297 to the capacity bound.

notes: Most actions are grounded in the evidence, but the guard and bound explanations could mislead an operator.
